newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN LEV ENDS FIRMER ON RISE IN DOLLAR SUPPLY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN LEV ENDS FIRMER ON RISE IN DOLLAR SUPPLY.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev closed between 2,800-3,000 per dollar, a touch firmer from 3,000-3,100 at midday due to a slight rise in dollar supply but still down from the morning's 2,650-2,800, dealers said.
"Banks, financials houses and exchange shops increased dollar sales in the afternoon which helped the lev rebound by 100-200 from midday lows," said a dealer.
However, market expectations of a further lev fall amid the current political instability and deepening economic crisis have not subsided.
"(Financial institutions) will probably continue to sell small dollar volumes to service pending lev payments, but it is generally expected that dollar supply would remain low," another dealer said.
Traders attributed the current low lev liquidity to central bank's decision to curb the inflow of levs to the interbank market.

The central bank temporarily barred commercial banks from using 30 percent of their minimum required reserves for emergency refinancing from January 30 in a bid to relieve pressure on the lev. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
